title_zh: 周报 | 英伟达、IBM联合费米实验室将推出模块化量子计算平台；Google Quantum AI等在百比特芯片实测测量情境性，实现量子-经典性能分离..
text_zh:
IBM宣布与NVIDIA、费米实验室合作，计划推出模块化量子计算平台
11月16日，IBM、NVIDIA和费米实验室计划开发一个模块化的量子计算联合设计平台，将量子处理器与加速经典计算系统集成。此次合作将涵盖量子-高性能计算集成、科学应用和硬件架构，同时IBM和NVIDIA还与Pasqal及开源社区合作开发QRMI，这是一种用于在Slurm工作流程中管理量子处理器的接口。IBM、理研和英伟达分别使用量子处理器和NVIDIA GPU模拟铁硫簇，其精度比早期实验提高了79倍。
来源：
https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-11-16-ibm,-fermilab,-and-nvidia-announce-plans-for-new-co-design-platform-to-accelerate-the-development-of-next-generation,-modular-quantum-computers
美国
Google Quantum AI等实测测量情境性实现量子
-
经典性能分离
本研究利用超导量子处理器，考察多玩家在无法通信且资源受限时的协调决策，证明量子测量的情境性可使任务成功率超过经典上限。研究人员先用少量量子比特实现魔方阵游戏，并通过违反贝尔
–科亨–斯佩克不等式量化情境性，随后实施多玩家格林伯格–霍恩–蔡林格游戏，另行求解二维隐藏线性函数问题。两类多体任务在保真度和系统规模上均取得进展。研究将情境性从基础量子特征转化为可实验检验的算法资源，并提出以此为基础评估量子处理器的基准方法。研究成果于11月19日发表于《Science》（科学）。
来源：
https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aec3042
伦敦宣布投入2200万英镑创新资金，1200万英镑用于量子产业集群
11月15日，伦敦市长萨迪克·汗宣布，通过地方创新伙伴基金向量子技术及生命科学领域的三个项目提供2200万英镑。其中，伦敦量子产业集群获1200万英镑，由伦敦大学学院、帝国理工学院和伦敦国王学院牵头，将支持企业开展技术验证、对接投资，并推动量子技术在医疗、交通、金融和能源等领域的应用。
来源：
https://www.london.gov.uk/mayor-london-announces-record-ps22m-new-innovation-funding-mark-start-london-life-sciences-week
卡塔尔与法国签署意向书，加强量子技术领域合作
11月15日，据Qatar Tribune报道，卡塔尔与法国签署意向书，加强在人工智能、数字化转型、创新及量子技术等新兴技术领域的合作。该协议由两国部长在2026年国际电信联盟全权代表会议期间签署。合作重点包括数字技能发展，法国数字事务部长还强调了在量子技术和数字战略自主方面的共同抱负。
来源：
https://www.qatar-tribune.com/article/264438/latest-news/qatar-and-france-sign-letter-of-intent-to-enhance-cooperation-in-digital-fields
卡塔尔通信与信息技术部与SignQuantum合作，推进量子安全准备
11月15日，卡塔尔通信与信息技术部（MCIT）已与SignQuantum签署合作协议，评估后量子网络安全应用并为量子计算相关风险做好准备。该协议涵盖知识共享及后量子密码学和抗量子数字签名的潜在应用场景探索，任何试点或部署均需单独审批。SignQuantum的解决方案结合了后量子数字签名与通过QANplatform区块链技术实现的抗量子时间戳，以保护数字记录的完整性和真实性。
来源：
https://medium.com/qanplatform/signquantum-and-qatars-ministry-of-communications-and-information-technology-collaborate-on-0deef533e315
土耳其与IQM签署协议，将于2027年部署54比特量子计算机
11月15日，据Turkiye today报道，土耳其科学技术研究委员会（TÜBİTAK）宣布已与IQM签署协议，在其国家科研基础设施上安装一台54量子比特超导量子计算机，预计于2027年投产。该安装项目旨在为国内大学、研究机构和私营部门团队提供主权计算能力，无需依赖外部云服务提供商，该安装将完全归TÜBİTAK所有，保留对硬件、执行数据和生成知识产权的本地控制权。
来源：
https://www.turkiyetoday.com/business/turkiye-bets-on-54-qubit-quantum-computer-to-break-into-worlds-top-15-3232444
AQSolotl宣布使用NVIDIA NVQLink集成测试，延迟低至6.94微秒
11月16日，AQSolotl宣布将NVIDIA NVQLink集成到其Chronos-Q量子控制平台的初步成果，连接NVIDIA DGX Spark时，最低往返延迟为6.94微秒。在1000次请求中，测试记录了中位延迟为8.02微秒，第99百分位延迟为9.01微秒，测量涵盖了通信和处理时间。AQSolotl计划利用该集成与其校准合作伙伴进一步测试GPU辅助量子校准工作流程，尽管初始延迟测试未涉及量子处理器。
来源：
https://www.aqsolotl.com/post/aqsolotl-reports-round-trip-latency-as-low-as-6-94-microseconds-with-nvidia-nvqlink
Saltgrain和NTT Research合作，开发大宇宙后量子属性加密技术
11月16日，Saltgrain、NTT Research和卡内基梅隆大学的研究人员合作开发基于大宇宙的后量子属性加密方案，支持细粒度的数据访问策略，并设计用来抵御量子攻击。密钥策略和密文策略方案采用基于格点的密码学，并支持灵活属性，多权威版本允许不同组织或部门独立签发凭据。Saltgrain平台上的集成测试已经启动，研究基准测试显示，在涉及1到4个属性的策略上，苹果M4 Pro MacBook Pro的解密时间为5.6–33.5毫秒。
来源：
https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261116477727/en/Saltgrain-and-NTT-Research-Unveil-the-First-Practical-Large-Universe-Post-Quantum-Attribute-Based-Encryption
IQM支持NVIDIA与Slurm集成，实现量子计算机可调度工作
11月16日，IQM宣布正在支持NVIDIA将量子处理单元（QPU）集成到Slurm工作负载管理器的工作，使量子计算机能够在HPC环境中与CPU和GPU并行调度。IQM合作伙伴MQSC开发了一款开源编排器，将Slurm的分层资源（HRES）与量子设备管理接口（QDMI）结合起来，用于管理对IQM系统的访问。IQM正在评估HRES与其混合计算配置的整合，并计划在升级Slurm安装时与HPC中心共同验证这一方法
。
来源：
https://iqm.tech/press-releases/iqm-supports-nvidias-work-to-make-quantum-computers-schedulable-in-slurm/
Altera与OQC和NVIDIA合作演示基于FPGA的量子系统控制器参考设计
11月16日，Altera、Oxford Quantum Circuits和NVIDIA开发基于FPGA的量子控制器参考设计，将OQC量子处理器与NVIDIA GPU连接起来。该设计集成了量子比特控制和读出功能，以降低控制硬件需求，而GPU则负责校准和基于机器学习的读出分类等任务。这一系统将在芝加哥的超级计算2026大会上展示，参考设计预计于2027年1月发布。
来源：
https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261116607546/en/Altera-Demonstrates-an-FPGA-based-Quantum-System-Controller-Reference-Design-in-Collaboration-with-OQC-and-NVIDIA
Liquid C2与Graphiant合作，共同推动非洲量子安全网络
11月16日，Liquid C2与Graphiant合作，为非洲企业提供一套受控的量子安全网络即服务（NaaS），结合后量子加密、安全连接和数据主权控制。该服务将通过加密连接、网络分段和集中式安全策略连接分支机构、数据中心、云环境和业务合作伙伴。该产品还包含针对AI和IoT流量的网络级控制，使组织能够限制目的地、监控数据路由并维护可审计的网络活动记录。
来源：
https://liquid.tech/about-us/news/liquid-c2-and-graphiant-launches-quantum-secure-network-as-a-service/
Classiq与Ventum Consulting合作，推动德国企业量子计算发展
11月16日，Classiq与Ventum Consulting合作，帮助德国企业开发量子计算策略，积累内部专业能力并识别潜在应用。此次合作结合Classiq的量子软件平台和应用开发能力，以及Ventum Consulting在业务战略和组织转型方面的经验。这些公司将与企业团队合作，评估用例，优先排序应用，并开发可在量子硬件和模拟器上测试的量子软件。
来源：
https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/16/3403326/0/en/classiq-and-ventum-consulting-partner-to-advance-enterprise-quantum-computing-in-germany.html
QTREX宣布收购GIS，以扩大量子互连生产
11月16日，QTREX宣布已从Nano Dimension Ltd.收购了Global Inkjet Systems Limited（GIS）。此次收购将关键生产控制带入内部，并扩大了QTREX为量子计算行业量产低温互连的能力。双方于2026年11月16日签署了购买协议并完成交易。根据协议，1600万美元基础对价以QTREX证券支付。GIS于2025年实现营收1130万美元，交割时持有1000万美元现金且无债务。
来源：
https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/16/3403576/0/en/qtrex-acquires-gis-to-scale-quantum-interconnect-production-adding-10-million-in-cash-and-a-business-with-11-3-million-in-revenue.html
Quantum Machines演示实时量子纠错解码，通信往返延迟约2.4微秒
11月16日，Quantum Machines通过NVIDIA NVQLink，将OPX1000量子控制系统与CUDA-Q纠错解码器连接，实现电路运行期间的实时解码与反馈。模拟错误数据测试显示，控制器与解码器的通信往返延迟约2.4微秒。码距为11时，单轮解码耗时0.56-0.67微秒。早期版本计划于12月向OPX1000用户开放安装。
来源：
https://www.quantum-machines.co/press-release/real-time-qec-decoding-opx1000-nvidia-cuda-q/
Infleqtion公布第三季度业绩报告，营收同比增长25%
11月16日，Infleqtion公布第三季度业绩，营收达910万美元，同比增长25%，创单季新高。按美国通用会计准则计算的运营亏损由上年同期670万美元扩大至3450万美元。公司维持全年营收至少4510万美元的预期。技术方面，其Sqale系统利用80个物理量子比特，在一次计算中演示了30个纠缠逻辑量子比特协同运行。
来源：
https://infleqtion.com/newsroom/announcements/infleqtion-reports-third-quarter-2026-record-revenue-results-achieves-30-logical-qubit-milestone-and-maintains-full-year-revenue-guidance/
QUDORA集成NVIDIA CUDA-Q，用于混合量子-经典应用
11月16日，QUDORA Technologies已将NVIDIA CUDA-Q集成到其软件开发套件中，使开发者能够构建混合量子-经典程序，并在其Qamelion量子模拟器上进行测试。Qamelion利用自适应噪声建模来模拟QUDORA计划中的离子阱硬件，使开发者能够研究量子噪声如何影响程序行为。该集成可通过QUDORA SDK实现，为CUDA-Q用户提供一个环境，在访问QUDORA的物理量子处理器之前开发和测试支持的应用程序。
来源：
https://qudora.com/news/qudora-to-advance-hybrid-quantum-classical-application-development-through-nvidia-cuda-q-integration/
酉术量子宣布完成天使轮融资，加速量子计算算法及产品迭代
11月17日，上海酉术量子科技有限公司（简称“酉术量子”）宣布完成天使轮融资。本轮新增投资方为云启资本、嘉铭浩春，老股东菡源资产、小苗朗程、启高资本持续加码。多维资本长期担任独家财务顾问。融资资金将主要用于原创量子算法研发、UnitaryLab量子科学计算平台及UnitarySpark异构计算产品迭代、AI与Agent驱动能力优化、量子硬件适配，以及科研和产业市场拓展。
来源：
https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/N3YsoAyjUK79k-8952OY3w
Qluster筹集470万欧元，用于开发新一代量子计算机
11月17日，Qluster是Laboratoire Kastler Brossel的衍生公司，宣布已筹集了470万欧元的种子前融资，由Quantonation牵头，用于开发围绕工业计算需求设计的光子量子计算机。该公司将利用这笔资金建立研发实验室，并招募实验物理、量子计算理论和建筑领域的专家。Qluster的目标是在2032年前实现中等规模量子计算机，并在2036年前实现大规模、容错的通用量子计算机。
来源：
https://www.quantonation.com/news/qluster-raises-e4-7-million-to-develop-a-new-generation-of-quantum-computers
IQM公布Halocene升级计划，向1000+量子比特扩展
11月17日，IQM宣布启动其Halocene的升级计划，为客户提供从现有150量子比特系统到超过1000个量子比特系统的路径。客户可以在现有的AI和HPC基础设施上运行混合量子-经典工作负载，并在无停机的情况下升级到更新的Halocene系统。该项目每次升级都包含HPC集成服务，并在此基础上建立在IQM此前在VTT、莱布尼茨超级计算中心和LUMI AI工厂等组织的部署基础上。
来源：
https://iqm.tech/press-releases/iqm-unveils-halocene-upgrade-program-at-sc26-creating-a-path-to-over-1000-qubits-while-accelerating-integration-with-ai-based-applications/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
Q.ANT发布NPU Gen 2+光子处理器，新增光学离散傅里叶变换
11月17日，Q.ANT在芝加哥SC26展会上发布其NPU Gen 2+光子处理器，新增光学离散傅里叶变换，以支持AI和高性能计算的新方法。该公司展示了一个语言模型，该模型运行在处理器上，同时搭配AMD GPU，利用光学计算取代了计算密集型注意力层。Q.ANT正在扩展其软件工具包以支持新功能，并计划在2027年下半年推出结合Gen 2和Gen 2+处理器的商用系统。
来源：
https://qant.com/news/q-ant-unveils-npu-gen-2-plus-photonic-fourier-transforms-power-large-language-model/
SAXON Q宣布推出Quantum Watchdog，用于检测量子计算机故障
11月17日，据QUANTUM INSIDER报道，SAXON Q宣布推出Quantum Watchdog，这是一套专利系统，用于检测量子计算机硬件故障并触发保护响应，预计于2027年初上线。该系统使用独立的经典处理器进行经过验证的测试计算，监控运行状况，并跨多个量子处理器比较结果。定制配置可将多达一半的处理时间用于安全检查，而完全认证版本预计将在未来几年内问世。
来源：
https://thequantuminsider.com/2026/11/17/saxon-q-announces-quantum-watchdog-to-detect-when-quantum-computers-fail/
QuiX Quantum与Artilux和Brillink合作，开发近室温光子量子探测器
11月17日，QuiX Quantum、Artilux和Brillink已为QSPAD项目争取到资金支持，这是一项为期36个月的荷台联合项目，旨在开发用于光子量子计算的集成单光子探测器。该项目将开发锗-硅（GeSi）单光子雪崩二极管阵列，设计为在室温或接近室温下工作，最低可达-40°C，并采用热电冷却。这些探测器将与QuiX Quantum的氮化硅光子电路集成，支持其向可扩展、容错光子量子系统的开发路线图。
来源：
https://www.einpresswire.com/article/957112016/quix-quantum-advances-industrial-foundations-for-fault-tolerant-quantum-computing-through-dutch-taiwanese-qspad-project
NEC与IBM日本合作，演示集成QKD和PQC通信
11月17日，NEC和IBM日本完成了日本首个集成量子安全通信系统的演示，该系统结合了量子密钥分发（QKD）和后量子密码学（PQC）。演示通过基于ETSI GS QKD 014的API将NEC的QKD设备与IBM的Quantum Safe Proxy连接起来，将QKD衍生的密钥材料与ML-KEM-768结合起来，以建立TLS流量保护密钥，并使用ML-DSA-44进行基于证书的认证。研究证明，合并后的架构能够通过代理层运行，无需对现有应用进行重大改动，并计划探索在银行系统以及金融机构与数据中心之间通信中的部署。
来源：
https://www.nec.com/en/press/202611/global_20261117_01.html
GenQ正在开发量子测量产品，加速量子技术商业化
11月17日，GenQ正在开发量子测量产品，旨在与现有基础设施配合，用于商业和政府应用，包括光网络监控。该公司宣布近期融资由Wonder Ventures和Offline Ventures共同领衔。GenQ由前SpaceX工程师海莉·温斯坦博士创立，团队汲取了NSA、波音和USC的经验，开发紧凑型室温产品。
来源：
https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/genq-transforms-how-quantum-can-be-used-today-302941783.html
SEALSQ签署意向书，拟收购澳大利亚量子安全企业QuintessenceLabs
11月18日，SEALSQ宣布与澳大利亚QuintessenceLabs签署非约束性意向书，拟以现金和股份收购其全部股权。若交易完成，SEALSQ可将安全芯片、公钥基础设施和后量子密码技术与对方的量子随机数生成、密钥管理和量子密钥分发技术整合。双方已进入60天独家尽调和谈判期，预计于2027年上半年完成交易，具体取决于最终协议和相关审批。
来源：
https://www.sealsq.com/investors/news-releases/sealsq-signs-a-loi-to-acquire-quintessencelabs-with-the-objective-of-creating-a-world-leader-in-the-vertical-quantum-security-stack
Alice&Bob更新路线图，计划2030年实现200个逻辑量子比特
11月18日，Alice&Bob公布更新后的模块化量子计算路线图，将2030年的目标提高一倍，计划用3600个物理猫量子比特构建200个逻辑量子比特。公司拟通过低温互连扩展处理器规模，计划在2028年实现6个逻辑量子比特，2032年达到1024个，2034年达到2048个。公司表示，现已分别运行三个处理器，并演示了构成逻辑量子比特所需的各项功能。
来源：
https://alice-bob.com/newsroom/alice-bob-accelerates-roadmap/
EigenOrbit

# Weekly Report | NVIDIA, IBM, and Fermilab to Launch Modular Quantum Computing Platform; Google Quantum AI and Collaborators Demonstrate Measurement Contextuality on Hundred-Qubit Chips, Achieving Quantum–Classical Performance Separation

## IBM Announces Plans for Modular Quantum Computing Co-Design Platform with NVIDIA and Fermilab

On November 16, IBM, NVIDIA, and Fermilab announced plans to develop a modular quantum computing co-design platform that integrates quantum processors with accelerated classical computing systems. The collaboration will span quantum–high-performance computing (HPC) integration, scientific applications, and hardware architecture. IBM and NVIDIA are also working with Pasqal and the open-source community to develop QRMI, an interface for managing quantum processors within Slurm workflows. IBM, RIKEN (理化学研究所), and NVIDIA separately used quantum processors and NVIDIA GPUs to simulate an iron–sulfur cluster, achieving accuracy 79× higher than earlier experiments.

## Google Quantum AI and Collaborators Experimentally Demonstrate Measurement Contextuality, Achieving Quantum–Classical Performance Separation

This study employed a superconducting quantum processor to investigate coordinated decision-making by multiple players who cannot communicate and have limited resources, demonstrating that quantum measurement contextuality can enable task success rates exceeding classical upper bounds. Researchers first implemented a magic-square game with a small number of qubits and quantified contextuality by violating Bell–Kochen–Specker inequalities, then implemented multi-player Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger (GHZ) games and separately solved a two-dimensional hidden linear functions problem. Both classes of many-body tasks showed progress in fidelity and system scale. The work transforms contextuality from a foundational quantum feature into an experimentally verifiable algorithmic resource, and proposes it as the basis for a benchmarking method to evaluate quantum processors. Results were published in *Science* on November 19.

**Source:**
https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aec3042

On November 15, London Mayor Sadiq Khan announced £22 million in funding for three projects in quantum technology and life sciences through the Local Innovation Partnership Fund. Of this, £12 million is allocated to the London Quantum Industry Cluster, led by University College London, Imperial College London, and King's College London. The funding will support companies in technology validation, investor matchmaking, and the deployment of quantum technologies across healthcare, transportation, finance, and energy.

The agreement was signed by ministers from both countries during the 2026 ITU Plenipotentiary Conference. Cooperation priorities include digital skills development; France's Minister for Digital Affairs emphasized shared ambitions in quantum technology and digital strategic autonomy.

On November 15, Qatar's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) signed a cooperation agreement with SignQuantum to assess post-quantum cybersecurity applications and prepare for risks associated with quantum computing. The agreement covers knowledge sharing and exploration of potential use cases for post-quantum cryptography and quantum-resistant digital signatures; any pilots or deployments will require separate approval. SignQuantum's solutions combine post-quantum digital signatures with quantum-resistant timestamping implemented via the QANplatform blockchain to protect the integrity and authenticity of digital records.

The installation aims to provide sovereign computing capacity to domestic universities, research institutions, and private-sector teams without reliance on external cloud service providers. The system will be fully owned by TÜBİTAK, retaining local control over hardware, execution data, and generated intellectual property.

On November 16, AQSolotl announced preliminary results from integrating NVIDIA NVQLink into its Chronos-Q quantum control platform, achieving a minimum round-trip latency of 6.94 µs when connected to an NVIDIA DGX Spark. Across 1,000 requests, tests recorded a median latency of 8.02 µs and a 99th-percentile latency of 9.01 µs; measurements encompass both communication and processing time. AQSolotl plans to use this integration with its calibration partners to further test GPU-assisted quantum calibration workflows, though the initial latency tests did not involve a quantum processor.

On November 16, researchers from Saltgrain, NTT Research, and Carnegie Mellon University jointly developed a large-universe post-quantum attribute-based encryption scheme that supports fine-grained data access policies and is designed to resist quantum attacks. Both key-policy and ciphertext-policy schemes employ lattice-based cryptography with flexible attributes; a multi-authority version allows different organizations or departments to independently issue credentials. Integration testing on the Saltgrain platform has begun, and research benchmarks show decryption times of 5.6–33.5 ms on an Apple M4 Pro MacBook Pro for policies involving 1–4 attributes.

## IQM Supports NVIDIA's Work to Make Quantum Computers Schedulable in Slurm

On November 16, IQM announced that it is supporting NVIDIA's effort to integrate quantum processing units (QPUs) into the Slurm workload manager, enabling quantum computers to be scheduled alongside CPUs and GPUs in HPC environments. IQM partner MQSC developed an open-source orchestrator that combines Slurm's Hierarchical Resources (HRES) capability with the Quantum Device Management Interface (QDMI) to manage access to IQM systems. IQM is evaluating the integration of HRES with its hybrid computing configurations and plans to jointly validate this approach with HPC centers when upgrading Slurm installations.

On November 16, Altera, Oxford Quantum Circuits (OQC), and NVIDIA developed an FPGA-based quantum controller reference design that connects OQC's quantum processor to NVIDIA GPUs. The design integrates qubit control and readout to reduce control hardware requirements, while GPUs handle tasks such as calibration and machine learning–based readout classification. The system will be demonstrated at Supercomputing 2026 (SC26) in Chicago, and the reference design is expected to be released in January 2027.

On November 16, Liquid C2 and Graphiant partnered to deliver a managed quantum-safe Network-as-a-Service (NaaS) for African enterprises, combining post-quantum encryption, secure connectivity, and data sovereignty controls. The service will connect branch offices, data centers, cloud environments, and business partners through encrypted connections, network segmentation, and centralized security policies. The offering also includes network-level controls for AI and IoT traffic, enabling organizations to restrict destinations, monitor data routing, and maintain auditable records of network activity.

On November 16, Classiq and Ventum Consulting partnered to help German enterprises develop quantum computing strategies, build internal expertise, and identify potential applications. The collaboration combines Classiq's quantum software platform and application development capabilities with Ventum Consulting's experience in business strategy and organizational transformation. The companies will work with enterprise teams to evaluate use cases, prioritize applications, and develop quantum software that can be tested on quantum hardware and simulators.

On November 16, QTREX announced the acquisition of Global Inkjet Systems Limited (GIS) from Nano Dimension Ltd. On November 16, Quantum Machines connected its OPX1000 quantum control system to a CUDA-Q error correction decoder via NVIDIA NVQLink, enabling real-time decoding and feedback during circuit execution. Tests using simulated error data showed a controller-to-decoder round-trip communication latency of approximately 2.4 µs. At code distance 11, single-round decoding takes 0.56–0.67 µs. On November 16, QUDORA Technologies integrated NVIDIA CUDA-Q into its software development kit, enabling developers to build hybrid quantum–classical programs and test them on its Qamelion quantum simulator. Qamelion uses adaptive noise modeling to simulate QUDORA's planned ion trap hardware, allowing developers to study how quantum noise affects program behavior. On November 17, Qluster, a spin-off from the Laboratoire Kastler Brossel, announced the raising of €4.7 million in pre-seed financing led by Quantonation, to develop a photonic quantum computer designed around industrial computing requirements. The company will use the funds to establish an R&D laboratory and recruit experts in experimental physics, quantum computing theory, and architecture. Qluster targets a medium-scale quantum computer by 2032 and a large-scale, fault-tolerant universal quantum computer by 2036.

On November 17, IQM announced the launch of its Halocene upgrade program, providing customers a path from existing 150-qubit systems to systems exceeding 1,000 qubits. Each upgrade in the program includes HPC integration services, building on IQM's prior deployments at VTT, the Leibniz Supercomputing Centre (LRZ), and the LUMI AI Factory.

On November 17, Q.ANT unveiled its NPU Gen 2+ photonic processor at SC26 in Chicago, adding an optical discrete Fourier transform to support new approaches in AI and high-performance computing. The company demonstrated a language model running on the processor alongside an AMD GPU, using optical computation to replace computationally intensive attention layers. Q.ANT is expanding its software toolkit to support the new capabilities and plans to introduce commercial systems combining Gen 2 and Gen 2+ processors in the second half of 2027.

On November 17, The Quantum Insider reported that SAXON Q announced Quantum Watchdog, a patented system for detecting quantum computer hardware failures and triggering protective responses, expected to go live in early 2027. The system uses an independent classical processor to run verified test computations, monitors operational health, and compares results across multiple quantum processors. Custom configurations can dedicate up to half of processing time to safety checks, while a fully certified version is expected to be available within the next few years.

On November 17, QuiX Quantum, Artilux, and Brillink secured funding for the QSPAD project, a 36-month Dutch–Taiwanese collaboration to develop integrated single-photon detectors for photonic quantum computing. The project will develop germanium-silicon (GeSi) single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) arrays designed to operate at or near room temperature, down to a minimum of −40 °C using thermoelectric cooling. The detectors will be integrated with QuiX Quantum's silicon nitride photonic circuits to support its development roadmap toward scalable, fault-tolerant photonic quantum systems.

On November 17, NEC and IBM Japan completed Japan's first demonstration of an integrated quantum-safe communications system combining quantum key distribution (QKD) and post-quantum cryptography (PQC). The demonstration connected NEC's QKD device to IBM's Quantum Safe Proxy via an ETSI GS QKD 014-compliant API, combining QKD-derived key material with ML-KEM-768 to establish TLS traffic protection keys and using ML-DSA-44 for certificate-based authentication. The demonstration showed that the combined architecture can operate through a proxy layer without major modifications to existing applications. On November 17, GenQ announced it is developing quantum measurement products designed to work alongside existing infrastructure for commercial and government applications, including optical network monitoring. The company announced a recent funding round co-led by Wonder Ventures and Offline Ventures. GenQ was founded by Dr. Hayley Weinstein, a former SpaceX engineer, and the team draws experience from the NSA, Boeing, and USC to develop compact, room-temperature products.

If completed, SEALSQ could integrate its secure chip, public key infrastructure, and post-quantum cryptography capabilities with QuintessenceLabs' quantum random number generation, key management, and quantum key distribution technologies. On November 18, Alice & Bob published an updated modular quantum computing roadmap, doubling its 2030 target to 200 logical qubits built from 3,600 physical cat qubits. The company plans to scale processors via cryogenic interconnects, targeting 6 logical qubits in 2028, 1,024 in 2032, and 2,048 in 2034. On November 18, EigenOrbit and collaborators including the University of Trieste (Italy) developed quantum-inspired orthogonal adapters for fine-tuning medical image classifiers. The adapters draw on the structure of reconfigurable beam-splitter circuits, reducing trainable parameters while preserving the Lipschitz upper bound of the original network. In tests on trichoscopy images for alopecia diagnosis, 63.8% of images were certifiably robust at an allowed perturbation radius of 36/255, compared with 31.6% for low-rank adaptation and 35.6% for full fine-tuning.

On November 18, the University of the Basque Country, LuxQuanta, Ciena, and multiple European research network organizations jointly demonstrated a hybrid quantum-safe network spanning approximately 8,000 km, connecting Chicago, Amsterdam, and the Basque region. The team combined quantum key distribution with post-quantum cryptography, used QuLore to centrally manage keys across heterogeneous nodes, and applied encryption at the optical transport layer, IPsec tunnel layer, and end-to-end application layer respectively.

The integration allows Slurm to check QPU availability, schedule jobs, manage access, and automatically release resources, supporting hybrid workflows that combine CPUs, GPUs, and quantum processors. On November 19, BMO announced the validation of quantum utility using IBM quantum computers to identify which variables in a dataset are most useful for machine learning. According to BMO, the method was co-developed with Democritus University of Thrace and uses approximately one-tenth to one-hundredth the data sample size required to achieve comparable quality to conventional feature selection techniques. BMO identified customer modeling, risk assessment, and more personalized banking services as potential applications.

On November 19, Seoul Economic Daily reported that SK Broadband plans to build a quantum-security testbed connecting Korea and Singapore by conducting demonstrations on international submarine cable routes, with additional connections to testbeds in Poland and Bulgaria. The project will combine quantum key distribution (QKD) for domestic and local overseas segments with post-quantum cryptography (PQC) for the long-haul Busan-to-Singapore segment. On November 20, Digital Today reported that the quantum secure direct communication (QSDC) system jointly developed by KT and LG Electronics has been verified, successfully transmitting image and text data encoded in quantum states and reconstructing the data at the receiver. Unlike QKD, which is used to share encryption keys, this system encodes the message itself in quantum states. The team transmitted 1,024-bit image data and reconstructed the original image at the receiver, then performed text transmission and reconstruction using the same equipment. KT plans to improve transmission rates and system stability, and to conduct validation over live fiber-optic networks.
